main_body: Beehive-shaped thatched hut: a large domed thatch roof (rows ~2-56) over a short clay wall with an arched doorway (rows ~57-77)
top_band: Thatch roof dome from row 2 to about row 55 at x=40. It is lighter, ringed with tiered courses (L 186/154/124 bands separated by dark L 95/69 lines), and is clearly wider than the wall below. It reads as a sloped top surface, like the reference roofs.
evidence: The roof is a big domed surface whose courses curve and overhang the wall. Under the eave the wall top is darkened (rows ~57-60), and the door is inset with a frame and dark interior. The front wall sits below the roof as a separate vertical face, with a stone plinth at the base. No isometric side face is drawn. This structure matches the reference houses, where the roof slope is the top and the wall is the front face.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5-6 tone steps with per-course dashes and dark-brown separator lines. The outline is tinted dark brown (5% neutral edge pixels), not a black sticker line. The wall has plank dashes and a gradient shadow under the eave, plus a stone plinth. It is weaker than the references: 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18, only 31 distinct colours, and 12% flat-fill coverage on the wall and door interior against 0% in the references. That is slightly lower, but the craft and structure are comparable.
